1. Install BlackYT

BlackYT is Android only. It needs Android 8.0 or newer. iPhone and iPad support is planned for later, with no release date.

  1. Open the public v0.3.1 release page, scroll to Assets, and download BlackYT-Android-v0.3.1.apk. Do not choose the GitHub source-code ZIP.
  2. Open Chrome's ⋮ → Downloads or Android Files → Downloads. Tap the APK once the download completes.
  3. If Android asks for permission, on a Pixel go to Settings → Apps → Special app access → Install unknown apps → Chrome → Allow from this source. If Files opened the APK, choose Files. These labels vary by phone; the permission is only for the app that opens the file. Return to Downloads and tap the APK again. You can revoke the permission after installation. See Google Pixel install-from-source help.
  4. Tap Install, then Open. Find the app named BlackYT. The older Chrome shortcut named BlackYT Phone needs Termux and is a separate legacy app.

Standard installation, including the owner's UK Pixel setup, does not need Developer options, USB debugging, root access, bootloader unlocking, or a custom certificate. USB debugging is only for developers installing or inspecting a test build. Do not disable Play Protect or ignore security warnings. If Android shows a Play Protect, unverified-developer, organization, work, or school block, stop and contact the maintainer or device administrator. Do not try to bypass it. See the Android developer verification FAQ.

While music plays, look for Android’s media controls. Their visibility depends on your notification and lock-screen settings. BlackYT needs internet access to search and stream, but does not need microphone, contacts, or photo access. No BlackYT or paid hosting account is needed. Mobile-data charges may apply through your carrier, and streaming uses battery. The app does not save songs for offline listening.

Try a short playback check

Play a song for about two minutes, lock the screen, and check that audio continues. If you added another song, you can also check whether it starts when the first finishes. An optional mobile-data check may use your data allowance.

2. Play your first song

  1. Tap the search box. Enter a song or artist, or paste a YT link, then tap Search.
  2. Music results only is checked initially. Uncheck it if a result you want is missing. Music classification depends on available YT metadata and is not guaranteed.
  3. Optionally enter comma-separated words in Include any words or Exclude any words. Include keeps a result when any included word appears. Exclude removes it when any excluded word appears. Matching uses the available title and channel text.
  4. Tap Play on a result to start it now, or Add to append it to the queue.
  5. Use Previous, Stop, Play/Pause, Next, and the seek bar in the player. Android notification and lock-screen controls use the native player session.

The queue lasts only for the current app session. Filter settings persist. There are no offline downloads and no sign-in.

3. Install future updates

  1. Finish listening first: an update stops the running app, and the queue is not saved permanently.
  2. Download the newer APK from the official BlackYT release page.
  3. Open it and choose Update or Install over the existing BlackYT. Do not uninstall first; filter settings normally stay when updating.
  4. If Android reports a signature conflict, stop and ask the maintainer. Releases need the same signing key to update in place.

Your current app does not update itself automatically. Never download a replacement from an unrelated website.

FAQ

Do I need Developer options, USB debugging, or a computer?

No for a normal installation. A phone and internet connection are enough. Those developer settings are only used when a developer installs or inspects a test build.

Why does Android ask to allow installs from Chrome?

Android asks you to allow the app that opened the APK to install it. On a Pixel, use Settings → Apps → Special app access → Install unknown apps → Chrome → Allow from this source. Choose Files instead if Files opened the APK. You can turn the permission off afterwards; labels vary on other phones.

What is the difference between Play and Add?

Play starts that song now. Add places it after songs already in the queue. Add does not start a song when nothing is playing; use the large Play button in Now Playing if you have only added songs. There is no automatic radio that keeps choosing songs.

Does the queue survive when I close BlackYT?

No. The queue belongs to the current app session and can clear when the app closes or is force-stopped. Search filters are saved on the phone.

Does BlackYT download songs or need a YT sign-in?

No. It streams while online and does not provide offline downloads. There is no BlackYT sign-in or hosting account. Your phone carrier may charge for mobile data.

Can I use this on an iPhone or iPad?

Not yet. The current app is Android only. An iOS version is planned, but there is no release date.

Can I install the update over an existing BlackYT?

Yes, install the newer release over the existing app. Updates must use the same signing key. If Android reports a signature conflict, do not uninstall; contact the maintainer first.

Does the v0.3.0 phone test mean v0.3.1 was physically tested?

No. The owner checked v0.3.0 on a Pixel 10 Pro XL. v0.3.1 changes wording and disclaimer on the same playback engine, but was not separately physically tested.

What if Android shows a security block?

Stop and contact the app maintainer or your device administrator. Do not turn off Play Protect or try to bypass the block. Read the Android developer verification FAQ for official information.

Troubleshooting

I cannot find the APK.

Open the public release link above and look under Assets for BlackYT-Android-v0.3.1.apk. In Chrome, check ⋮ → Downloads; in Files, check Downloads. Do not use the source-code ZIP.

“App not installed” or “Problem parsing the package”.

Check that the phone runs Android 8.0 or newer and that the whole APK finished downloading. Download the exact APK again. If the message continues, stop and contact the maintainer with the phone model and exact error.

Play Protect, unverified-developer, work, or school warning.

Stop. Do not disable protections or bypass the warning. Ask the maintainer or device administrator for help.

Search shows no results or misses a song.

Check your connection, try a shorter song or artist name, uncheck Music results only, and clear or broaden the include/exclude words. Exclude words remove a result if any one matches and take priority when both fields contain the same word.

A song starts but there is no sound.

Check media volume, mute, Bluetooth, headphones, and whether Android routed audio to another device. Try Play/Pause and a different result.

HTTP 403 or playback stops after changing networks.

Check that the phone is online and tap Retry current song for a fresh stream link. Try another result if that song remains unavailable. Some items are restricted, and YT can change its service.

Playback stops when I lock the screen.

Reopen BlackYT and resume. If it keeps happening, check BlackYT only under Settings → Apps → BlackYT → App battery usage. On Pixel this may be labelled Allow background usage. Keep the general battery setting at its recommended value; do not disable optimization globally. Android's battery guidance explains app-specific background settings.

The queue is empty or the next song does not start.

Add puts a track at the end; it does not start an empty queue. Tap Play on one result, then Add more. Next advances to the next item in the queue.

My queue vanished.

The queue is session-only. Force-stopping the app, restarting the phone, or Android ending its process can clear it; filter settings are saved separately.

Android says the update cannot be installed.

Do not uninstall the working copy if Android reports a signing conflict. Updates require the same signing key. Contact the maintainer with the exact message.

I see both BlackYT and BlackYT Phone.

BlackYT is the native app. BlackYT Phone is the old Chrome shortcut that relies on Termux; the native app does not need it.

Still need help?

Open a BlackYT support issue. Tell us your phone model, Android version, the exact message and the step you reached. A GitHub account is needed to post an issue, but not to download the app.

Do not post passwords, signing keys, account tokens, private messages or complete stream links. Cover personal details in screenshots. Search your phone’s Settings for “Android version” if you need to find it.

About BlackYT

BlackYT is an independent educational project. Its creator uses it to listen to songs they wrote and perform. The project aims to help students explore music regardless of socioeconomic circumstances, with fewer advertising interruptions and low running costs.

Disclaimer

BlackYT is an independent, unofficial project for educational use. Use it lawfully and respect copyright, licences, creators' rights, and applicable platform terms. Educational status is not permission to break the law or bypass rights or restrictions. You are responsible for the material you access and how you use it.

YT can change its service and availability at any time. BlackYT may stop working as a result. No affiliation or permission to use third-party material is implied.

Device test history and technical notes

The signed v0.3.0-native APK was installed on the Pixel 10 Pro XL and its installed APK hash matched the release file. Five unit checks passed, release lint reported zero errors with routine warnings, and a native Googlevideo audio request returned HTTP 200. The owner confirmed audible playback, playback with the screen locked, and automatic playback of the next queued song while locked. The owner also confirmed v0.3.0-native playback on mobile data with USB unplugged. v0.3.1 updates wording and disclaimer only on the same playback engine; it has not been physically tested on the Pixel. These checks do not establish support for every Android device.

Audio streams directly from YT to the phone; the Mac and Termux are not playback dependencies. Android's Media3 background playback guidance describes the app's playback approach.

Mascot artwork and prompt

Original artwork created for BlackYT using the built-in image-generation tool. The open wings and flowing notes represent the enjoyment of music without barriers.

Prompt: Original friendly joyous black songbird mascot for BlackYT, understated headphones, wings open as if dancing, a few colorful musical notes flowing freely. Polished expressive illustration, warm welcoming inclusive expression, rich deep green and lime brand accents, full figure centered with clean thumbnail-readable silhouette and comfortable margins. Genuine transparent background. No locks, walls, broken barriers, text, logos, watermark, or imitation of known mascots.
